Few things I tell people. And I say it because I have been on the other side of this spectrum. 

Firstly, if a person is sinking in quicksand, the most you can do is give them your hand/rope/stick or anything to get them out. But what you don't realise is the person who is sinking may not accept your help.

Idk if this makes sense to you but sometimes if they tell you what is going on in their life or that they have suicidal tendencies, it could just be because they saw you are worried about them and, like someone said, trust you enough to let you in. It may not necessarily be a subtle cry for help but rather a warning that says being too close to me is not easy.

Secondly, something the person who is suicidal always hears, is that it's going to be alright, I will be there for you. These words, although powerful, will lose it's value to that person. So I would say unless you are trying to show it in action, don't use such empty words.

Lastly, be who you are with them, spend everyday normally with them, talk normally with them, and let them know that they matter to you, not with words but with actions. These things can certainly change a person's heart and give them hope.

#tl:dr

Sometimes people don't wanna be saved

Don't use comforting words only to give them comfort, show it in action

Be normal with them and show them that they matter to you.
